summary: Planned maintenance simulation lets you test a near-zero-downtime maintenance event on an Enterprise Plus primary instance without applying an update.
extended_definition: Planned maintenance simulation lets you test a near-zero-downtime maintenance event on an Enterprise Plus primary instance without applying an update.

supporting_pages.title: Availability in Cloud SQL \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: Maintenance , which includes the following operations with sub-second downtime: Automatic maintenance that Cloud SQL performs every quarter Self-service maintenance that you can initiate at any time Maintenance simulation that you can initiate to test the sub-second downtime behavior Minor version upgrade Perform a minor version upgrade on a MySQL 8.0 instance with sub-second downtime For PostgreSQL instances, minor version upgrades are part of automatic maintenance and happen with sub-second downtime Edition upgrade Perform an in-place upgrade to Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition Enable data cache You can enable or disable data cache as frequently as needed Instance scaling Scale-up: Increase the compute size (vCPU, memory) of your Cloud SQL instance as frequently as needed Scale-down: Reduce the compute size (vCPU, memory) of your Cloud SQL instance infrequently Note: If you scale down your instance more than once during a three-hour period, then only the first scale down event benefits from near-zero downtime.

Planned operations with near-zero downtime For planned operations such as maintenance or some instance reconfigurations, Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition offers near-zero downtime for primary instances with no application changes or proxy requirements.
With a 99.99% uptime SLA and near-zero downtime for several planned operations, Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition offers greater resilience and business continuity for your applications.
